docs.text: Pizza Ontology A pizza ontology built with OntoBoard from ontology design patterns, following the eXtreme Design methodology. This site is published from the docs/ folder of this repository by GitHub Actions, every time main changes. Getting the ontology What Where Browse https://ebrahimnorouzi.github.io/pizza-ontology/pizza.owl Edit file src/ontology/pizza-edit.owl Released file pizza.owl Documentation The ontology's documentation page Edit the edit file , never the released one: the released file is produced by the build and is overwritten by it. Turning this site on GitHub does not publish Pages until it is asked. Once, in the repository's Settings > Pages , set the source to Deploy from a branch and choose the gh-pages branch - the workflow creates that branch the first time it runs. The site then appears at https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/ .

docs.text: Editing Pizza Ontology With Protege and OntoBoard Open src/ontology/pizza-edit.owl . Work on the OntoBoard tab, or in Protege's own views. Run OntoBoard > Project > Build... and choose test before you commit. It runs the same checks the repository's CI runs. Identifiers New terms are minted from the range allocated to you in src/ontology/pizza-idranges.owl . Give each editor their own range - OntoBoard > Project > ID ranges... - so two people never mint the same identifier for different things. What the checks mean Target What it does reason Runs the reasoner and writes its conclusions into pizza.owl report ROBOT's quality report, failing on anything at ERROR sparql_test The checks in src/sparql/ validate_profile That the ontology is still OWL 2 DL test All four

docs.text: Releasing Pizza Ontology A release is a frozen copy that other ontologies can import and that will not change under them. This project numbers its releases semantically: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH . Make sure test passes: OntoBoard > Build and release > Build... , target test . OntoBoard > Build and release > Release... , Semantic version , the next version. It stamps the version IRI https://ebrahimnorouzi.github.io/pizza-ontology/pizza/<version> , with owl:versionInfo and owl:priorVersion , and writes releases/<version>/pizza.owl and the published pizza.owl . Publish the release under its IRIs: copy pizza.owl to docs/pizza.owl , and releases/<version>/pizza.owl to docs/pizza/<version> - with no extension, as in the version IRI. This site serves them at those addresses. OntoBoard > Build and release > Documentation... , Write it to docs/ontology , Include the WebVowl diagram ticked. It documents the release you just made, and its changelog compares that release with the one before it - which has to be online already, as step 3 of the last release put it. Commit all of it, tag the commit v<version> , and push. This site is republished from main . A version IRI cannot be taken back once somebody has imported it, so the release step refuses to overwrite a release that already exists.

docs.text: Competency questions, answered Each query in this folder run against the released pizza.owl (reasoned with ELK), with OntoBoard > ROBOT > SPARQL... These answers are regenerated on every release. CQ1: What are the base and the toppings of the Margherita on the menu? cq1-components.rq - 3 row(s) kind part base thin and crispy base topping mozzarella topping topping tomato topping CQ2: Which pizzas on the menu have mozzarella on them? cq2-pizzas-with-topping.rq - 5 row(s) pizza diavola (menu item) funghi (menu item) hawaiian (menu item) margherita (menu item) quattro formaggi (menu item) CQ3: Which pizzas are spicy? Nobody asserted it: the reasoner puts them under SpicyPizza. cq3-spicy-pizzas.rq - 1 row(s) pizza diavola CQ4: Which pizzas on the menu are vegetarian? cq4-vegetarian-pizzas.rq - 3 row(s) pizza funghi (menu item) margherita (menu item) quattro formaggi (menu item) CQ5: How hot is each pizza on the menu? cq5-spiciness.rq - 5 row(s) pizza level diavola (menu item) hot funghi (menu item) mild hawaiian (menu item) mild margherita (menu item) mild quattro formaggi (menu item) mild CQ6: How much does each pizza on the menu cost, and in which currency? cq6-prices.rq - 5 row(s) pizza amount currency diavola (menu item) 10.50 euro funghi (menu item) 9.50 euro hawaiian (menu item) 10.00 euro margherita (menu item) 8.50 euro quattro formaggi (menu item) 11.00 euro CQ7: Which pizzas cost less than 10 euros? cq7-cheaper-than-10.rq - 2 row(s) pizza amount margherita (menu item) 8.50 funghi (menu item) 9.50

docs.text: Requirements (eXtreme Design scoping) eXtreme Design (XD) builds an ontology in small iterations. Each iteration takes one user story, turns it into competency questions (CQs), finds the ontology design pattern (ODP) that answers them, specialises that pattern, and tests the result against the CQs before the next iteration starts. Each iteration here ends in a release with its own semantic version. User stories Story As a... I want to... so that... Iteration S1 pizzeria owner describe what each pizza on my menu is made of - its base and toppings customers can see the ingredients 1 (v0.2.0) S2 customer know which pizzas suit a vegetarian diet and how hot each one is I can choose quickly 2 (v0.3.0) S3 pizzeria owner give every pizza on the menu a price in a currency the menu can be printed and compared 3 (v0.4.0) Competency questions CQ Question Story Answered by Test CQ1 What are the base and the toppings of a given pizza? S1 docs/cq/cq1-components.rq src/sparql/cq1_every_pizza_has_a_base.rq CQ2 Which pizzas have a given topping, e.g. mozzarella? S1 docs/cq/cq2-pizzas-with-topping.rq src/sparql/cq2_toppings_are_toppings.rq CQ3 Which pizzas are spicy? S1 docs/cq/cq3-spicy-pizzas.rq (needs the reasoner) reasoned release CQ4 Which pizzas are vegetarian? S2 docs/cq/cq4-vegetarian-pizzas.rq src/sparql/cq4_vegetarian_pizzas_have_no_meat.rq CQ5 How hot is a given pizza? S2 docs/cq/cq5-spiciness.rq src/sparql/cq5_every_pizza_has_a_spiciness_level.rq CQ6 How much does a given pizza cost, and in which currency? S3 docs/cq/cq6-prices.rq src/sparql/cq6_every_pizza_has_a_price.rq CQ7 Which pizzas cost less than 10 euros? S3 docs/cq/cq7-cheaper-than-10.rq - Contextual statements A pizza has exactly one kind of base and one or more toppings. Toppings are grouped as cheese, meat, vegetable and fruit toppings; some are spicy. A menu item is a particular pizza with its own base, toppings, diet category, spiciness level and price. Reasoning requirements SpicyPizza is defined , not asserted: any pizza with at least one spicy topping. The reasoner must place Diavola under it, because spicy salami is a spicy topping. CheesyPizza likewise: any pizza with at least one cheese topping. Everything stays in OWL 2 EL, so ELK - the reasoner the in-process build uses - classifies it, and in OWL 2 DL, which validate_profile checks. Patterns chosen Each chosen in OntoBoard → ROBOT → Pattern library... by searching for the CQ's words. The library answers with patterns whose own competency questions match. All three are sound: the library's reasoner check ( patterns/soundness.tsv in OntoBoard) found each consistent with no unsatisfiable class. Iteration Pattern (library id) Its own CQs Specialised as 1 Componency ( componency ) What are the components of this entity? What is this entity a component of? Pizza , PizzaBase , PizzaTopping ⊑ Object ; hasBase , hasTopping ⊑ hasComponent 2 Classification ( classification ) What concept classifies this entity? What entities are classified by this concept? DietCategory , SpicinessLevel ⊑ Concept ; menu items isClassifiedBy vegetarian , mild , hot 3 Price ( price ) How much does a given item cost, and in which currency? MenuPrice ⊑ Price ; euro a Currency ; hasPrice , hasCurrency , hasValue Source: the ontology design patterns are from the ODP portal (ontologydesignpatterns.org), bundled with OntoBoard; each import keeps the pattern's own IRIs.
